title: Auto Insurance

questions.prompt: Which auto insurance coverage protects you if you cause an accident that injures another person?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Liability coverage pays for injuries and property damage you cause to others.

questions.prompt: The part of auto insurance that covers damage to your own car from a crash is called ___ coverage.
Which coverage pays if your car is stolen? (word: collision or comprehensive)

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The third number is the property damage limit (in thousands).
questions.prompt: In a split limit policy of 100/300/50, what does the third number (50) represent?
Policy limit 30/60/15. At‑fault accident causes $20,000 property damage. How much does insurance pay? (number only, no $)

options: The insured pays before the insurer pays
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The deductible is the amount the insured pays before the insurer pays.

hints: You pay more if a claim occurs.
questions.prompt: If you choose a higher deductible, your premium will generally be ___.
Collision damage $2,800, deductible $300. How much does the insurer pay? (number only, no $)
Your car is totaled with ACV $9,000 and $1,000 deductible. The insurer will pay:
Which factor typically increases auto insurance premiums the most?
options: Time of day the car is driven
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A poor driving record with accidents increases premiums significantly.

questions.prompt: If another driver is at fault, their ___ insurance should pay for your car damage.
You have $500 collision deductible and cause $1,200 damage to your car. How much do you pay out‑of‑pocket? (number only, no $)

instructions: Answer all questions. For fill‑in‑the‑blank and short‑answer, use one word, letter, or number only.
